title: Machine Learning
weightage: ~12–20 marks (roughly 8–12 questions) per GATE DA paper (2024–2026); the highest-weightage core subject alongside Probability & Statistics
summary: The largest technical section of GATE DA: expect numerical questions on regression (OLS/ridge), logistic/naive Bayes/kNN computations, SVM margins, decision-tree entropy/information gain, k-means/hierarchical clustering traces and PCA eigen-computations, plus conceptual MCQ/MSQ on bias-variance, cross-validation and neural networks.
notesGuide: 1) Download the free ISLP PDF (statlearning.com -> ISLP download page) and use it as the primary text: Ch 3 (linear regression), Ch 4 (logistic, LDA, naive Bayes, kNN), Ch 5 (LOOCV/k-fold), Ch 6.2 (ridge), Ch 8 (trees), Ch 9 (SVM), Ch 10 (neural nets), Ch 12 (PCA, k-means, hierarchical). 2) Download Stanford CS229 main_notes.pdf for the math layer (normal equations, logistic MLE, GDA vs naive Bayes, SVM dual, backprop, bias-variance). Keep Bishop PRML (free Microsoft PDF) only as a reference for LDA (Ch 4) and PCA (Ch 12). 3) For quick 1-page reads per algorithm, the Cornell CS4780 (Kilian Weinberger) HTML lecture notes are excellent - print/save kNN, naive Bayes, logistic, linear regression, SVM, bias-variance, decision trees, neural nets notes. 4) Make your own short notes as one A4 sheet per algorithm with fixed headings: model/hypothesis, loss/objective, closed form or update rule, key hyperparameters, effect of hyperparameters on bias/variance, a tiny hand-worked numeric example (e.g. 4-point k-means, 3-point OLS, entropy of a 2-class split), and 'GATE traps'. 5) Maintain a separate formula sheet: OLS beta=(X^T X)^-1 X^T y, ridge (X^T X+lambda I)^-1 X^T y, sigmoid/log-odds, entropy & information gain & Gini, SVM margin 2/||w||, LOOCV formula for linear smoothers, PCA = eigenvectors of covariance, variance explained ratios, linkage definitions. 6) After each topic, solve the matching GATE Overflow tag page questions and add every mistake to an 'error log' section at the bottom of that topic's sheet. Watch the StatQuest video first if a concept doesn't click, then return to ISLP.
